A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPT point-cloud synthesis work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and substantial supplementary additions in v4.

before.justification: V3 reports original reconstruction, generation, timing, downsampling and inversion results, including Tables 1–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds partial-view, multi-class, cross-class transfer, sensitivity and generation experiments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The IPT construction, IP-Encoder, joint CD/IPT loss and principal IP-VAE pipeline are retained. Figure S.6 adds a preliminary procedural extension: training a diffusion model on VAE latent embeddings of airplane IPTs, then converting generated IPTs with the existing IP-Encoder.

E1.justification: V3 primarily evaluates three ShapeNet classes separately. V4 adds MNIST point-cloud reconstruction and generation, joint reconstruction across ShapeNet13's thirteen classes, and partial-view completion on GenRe chairs and cars. These substantially broaden the represented data and task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Point Straight Flows (PSF) to the inference-time comparison, reporting 0.040 seconds on GPU. PSF already appeared in v3's generation-quality comparison, but was absent from its timing table. The established comparator sets in Tables 1 and 4 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include varying direction counts from 4 to 128 at fixed spatial resolution, training downsamplers producing 32–512 points, reconstructing 4096-point clouds, and training with random rotations on MNIST. Partial-view and cross-class tests also evaluate previously trained models without retraining. These expand the evaluation design; the retained main reconstruction and inversion training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds cross-class failure analysis, direction-count and downsampling-cardinality sensitivity studies, and a qualitative rotation-augmentation experiment (Tables S.3–S.5 and Figure S.5). Figure 3 supplements the retained interpolation example with a less similar pair of airplanes. The earlier loss and inversion-scale ablations remain present.

E5.justification: Both versions already report ± values in reconstruction and inversion tables. V4 adds no run counts, seed information, definitions of those uncertainty values, confidence intervals or significance tests. Its checklist describes selective error-bar reporting without establishing a changed statistical practice.

E6.justification: Tables S.2–S.6 and the new MNIST and diffusion figures add substantial numerical and qualitative results, including cross-class failures. Reported IP-Encoder/IP-VAE training times change from 2 hours/6 hours to 30 minutes/15 minutes, identified as corrections in the changelog. Tables 1, 2, 4, 5 and the original appendix inversion values are unchanged; Table 6 redisplays selected inversion results. Section 4.4 also corrects the reported ranking of backpropagation versus the IP-Encoder.

T1.justification: Theorem 2 now explicitly requires q > 0 in both the main text and proof appendix, excluding undefined fractions. The proof arguments remain unchanged. Section 3.1 also revises its qualification about exact-IPT properties to exempt injectivity, without supplying an additional proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions and concluding core summary retain the same claims: an efficient image-to-point-cloud pipeline, an expressive representation supporting interpolation and out-of-distribution use, and injectivity with applicability to arbitrary dimensions. Added evidence and revised qualifications do not redefine these principal contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 reverses v3's incorrect statement that backpropagation reconstructs worse than the IP-Encoder, explaining its superior clean-IPT reconstruction while retaining limitations for generated or noisy IPTs. Section 5 replaces the infinite-directions-only caveat with difficulty choosing directions and resolution. New supplementary discussions identify cross-class generalisation failures, fixed-output scalability limitations and possible learned rotation equivariance.

D1.justification: V4 adds a public implementation URL and BSD-3-Clause license statement, specific GPU/CPU/memory information, and clarification of fixed direction ordering. Table 4 newly identifies comparison results as sourced from the respective papers. Training-time disclosures are corrected, while the principal architecture diagrams and retained experimental hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds a structure-from-motion analogy and references concerning ECT stability, learnable positional encodings, molecular applications, transformers and graph-generation evaluation. These broaden the surrounding context while retaining the central positioning relative to ECT inversion and existing point-cloud generators. Publication updates to already cited works do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: V4 clarifies and condenses several passages, expands explanations of direction ordering and practical inversion, and renames the downsampling and inversion subsections. It adds acknowledgments, a checklist, appendix contents and a changelog. The main scientific section order and overall narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds five supplementary tables and three supplementary figures. It moves v3's interpolation Figure C.4 into the main text as Figure 3 and adds a second example; new Table 6 redisplays existing appendix results. Figure 2 is enlarged and relocated, and takeaway boxes and other displays are reformatted. These are substantial display changes beyond pagination.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens empirical support and clarifies applicability through partial-view, multi-class, sensitivity and explicit failure experiments. It also corrects an inversion conclusion that contradicted the retained numerical evidence and resolves the misleading infinite-directions limitation. Code-access and hardware disclosures improve transparency. Some additions remain preliminary, and the differing 256-point results in Tables 5 and S.5 are not reconciled, but these reporting limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and interpretation.
